Given the normal platelet count, coagulation profile, bleeding time, and factor assays, the persistent mucocutaneous bleeding suggests a qualitative platelet defect not detected by standard tests, such as Glanzmann thrombasthenia or Bernard-Soulier syndrome, though the normal smear makes Bernard-Soulier less likely.
